_readme: Shape of the classifier prompt secrets. The real instructions are
operational secrets: this repo is public, and the exact BLOCK/ALLOW rules
would double as an evasion manual. Keep the real values in GitHub secrets
(Settings -> Secrets -> Actions); the Supabase deploy workflow syncs them
to the Edge Function. Each value is a full system prompt (min 40 chars,
enforced by the worker's loader).
TWO secrets, not one. MODERATION_PROMPTS carries message, photo and
verification. MODERATION_PROMPTS_BUSINESS optionally carries storefront and
impersonation. The split exists because a GitHub secret is write-only: you
cannot read the working value back to append to it, and requiring all five
in one place would mean retyping three live, tuned prompts to add a fourth.
Either secret may carry either set; the business one wins on a clash.
Only message, photo and verification are REQUIRED. Absent business keys
pause exactly those two queues and say so in the worker report, rather than
stopping moderation entirely.
TWO REASONS, ONE OF THEM ENGLISH. The verification and storefront verdicts
each carry `reason` AND `reason_en`, both required by the worker's schema.
`reason` is what the person is shown, and the worker appends a per-item line
to the content naming the BCP 47 tag their phone reports (profiles.locale);
a null locale asks for English, silently, never for a nearest guess.
`reason_en` is the same sentence in English and is shown to nobody: it is
what makes an appeal adjudicable by a founder who does not read the other
language, and it is what the 'uncertain' storefront mail quotes.
TONE RULES FOR MODEL-WRITTEN TEXT, which the app cannot enforce after the
fact: no em dashes, never an accusation, say what to do differently, and
sentence case. Write in the same plain register in either language; if the
model cannot write the named language well, it writes `reason` in English
rather than badly.
message: System prompt for first-message moderation on a strictly platonic travel app. Must instruct the model to return an allow/block verdict per the MessageVerdict schema, define what gets blocked (romantic/sexual advances, harassment, spam/scams, off-platform payment lures) and what stays allowed (friendly platonic plans), and say which way to lean on ambiguity.
photo: System prompt for profile/chat photo moderation (18+ app, platonic). Must instruct the model to return an allow/block verdict per the PhotoVerdict schema and define blocked imagery vs normal travel photos, including how to treat readable personal contact info.
verification: System prompt for selfie-vs-profile-photos plausibility review. Must instruct the model to return an approve/reject verdict per the VerificationVerdict schema, with short non-accusatory user-facing reasons on reject. Must require BOTH `reason` (in the language named by the per-item line the worker appends, English when none is named) and `reason_en` (always English, the same sentence, read only by the founder adjudicating an appeal). No em dashes; say what to do differently rather than what went wrong with the person.
storefront: System prompt for the business storefront check: two live photos (a wide shot from the street and a close shot of the sign) against a claimed name, category and city. Must return approve/reject/uncertain per the StorefrontVerdict schema, must treat translation, transliteration and trading names as normal rather than suspicious, must call out screenshots, photos of a screen, stock imagery and renders, and must prefer 'uncertain' over 'reject' whenever the photos are simply hard to read. Must require BOTH `reason` (in the owner's own language, per the line the worker appends) and `reason_en` (always English: the 'uncertain' branch mails it to the founder, who finishes the call by hand). No em dashes, never an accusation about somebody's livelihood, and always a next step.
impersonation: System prompt for the business impersonation scan, run on the first report. Given a listing's name, category, city, description, links and posts plus one report, must return impersonation_plausible per the ImpersonationVerdict schema. Must weigh the report without treating it as evidence on its own, because a competitor can file one, and must lean towards not plausible when the listing is merely thin or badly written.
